events.summary: President Michael Sentonas sold 241,944 shares on 2026-09-30 at weighted-average prices of $262.71-$267.96, about $64.2 million in total, under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-07-01. 12,920 of the shares came from exercising 2016 stock options with a $1.665 strike. His directly held shares fell from 1,487,461 to 1,245,517 (about 16% of his direct stake sold). The matching Form 144 (2026-09-30) also lists an earlier sale of 49,863 shares on 2026-09-21 for $11,555,359.29. Same evening, CEO George Kurtz reported selling 20,000 shares on 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-01 for about $5.3 million (10,000 a day, about 0.26% of his direct stake). That plan was adopted 2026-01-06. He still holds 7,551,504 shares directly plus 400,000 through a family trust.
events.why_it_matters: All sales are flagged as 10b5-1 (instructions set up in advance, after a cooling-off period), so they say little about management's current view. Kurtz has followed a steady 10,000-shares-a-day pattern all through the filings window. The size is notable, though: the pipeline counts 79 open-market sales worth about $210.4 million in the filings window and no purchases. The CFO's sale is the biggest (see background event). Nobody has sold outside a plan, so the insider thesis breaker did not fire.

events.summary: Potomac Investments LP, which the form lists with the relationship 'Director', filed notice of a planned sale of 82,000 shares (about $21.8 million) through Goldman Sachs, approximately on 2026-10-01. The notice says the sale is under a 10b5-1 selling plan dated 2026-06-25. The same form lists earlier sales of 20,000 shares on 2026-09-01, 20,000 on 2026-08-04 and 5,000 on 2026-07-01. The shares came from a distribution by an Accel growth fund. The director behind the entity is not named in what we read.
events.why_it_matters: A Form 144 is a notice of a planned sale, not proof of the sale. This one fits a pre-planned, recurring selling pattern, not a sudden exit.

events.type: background: quarterly earnings (Q2 FY2027) with raised guidance
events.summary: Q2 FY27 (quarter ended 2026-07-31): revenue $1.47B (+26% YoY), subscription revenue $1.40B (+27%), ending ARR $5.84B (+25%), net new ARR $332.8M (+51% YoY, a record), GAAP net income $5.3M ($0.01/share), non-GAAP EPS $0.31, operating cash flow $530.3M, free cash flow $377.4M. Results beat consensus: revenue $1.44B, EPS $0.29, ARR $5.79B expected. Full-year FY27 revenue guidance went up to $5,991.1-$6,011.1M (consensus was $5.94B) and net new ARR growth guidance to 34% at the midpoint. The stock rose as much as 12% in after-hours trading.
events.why_it_matters: This is the most recent hard evidence for the thesis that customers keep adding modules and ARR growth is speeding up, not slowing. It is also the base the market is now pricing from.

events.summary: CFO Burt Podbere sold 480,000 shares on 2026-09-24 at about $259-$264, about $125.5 million in total (filed 2026-09-25). Of these, 320,000 came from his direct holding, which fell from 662,936 to 342,936, and 160,000 came from four family trusts. Direct sales are under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-06-24. After the sales, the accounts that traded still held about 669,000 shares, and other trust holdings are listed with no transactions. The pipeline's '89.9% of holdings sold' figure is a parsing artefact: it mixes direct and trust lines. Calculated from the Form 4 lines, he sold roughly 42% of the shares in the accounts that traded, and less once the other trusts are counted.
events.why_it_matters: This is the largest single insider sale in the window, by the executive who knows the numbers best. It was pre-planned (plan adopted three months earlier) and came after the stock had roughly doubled, so it is most likely diversification. Still, it is worth knowing about.

events.summary: CrowdStrike put its Falcon platform on the OpenAI Marketplace. Eligible OpenAI enterprise customers can pay for Falcon with part of their existing OpenAI spending commitments. The release also mentions Falcon Guardian (runtime protection for OpenAI Codex agents) and a FAIRR readiness service. No pricing or customer numbers were disclosed. Earlier the same month, CrowdStrike bought XM Cyber technology assets on 2026-09-08 and paid with 2,118,022 newly issued shares; an S-3ASR resale shelf for those shares was filed 2026-09-11.
events.why_it_matters: It is a new sales channel tied to the 'AI needs security' story management credits for faster growth. Its revenue effect is not disclosed.

events.type: background: 4-for-1 stock split (and Q1 FY27 results)
events.summary: On 2026-06-03, alongside its Q1 FY27 results, the board approved a four-for-one stock split. Shares began trading on a split-adjusted basis on 2026-07-02. That is why today's price (about $270) looks far lower than the $400-plus prices quoted in older articles, and why the 52-week low of $85.68 is a split-adjusted number.
events.why_it_matters: A split changes the number of slices, not the size of the pie, so it does not change the company's value. Santi needs to know it so he does not misread old prices.

why_chain.text: Friday 2026-10-02: CRWD rose 1.48% to $270.04. The model splits that into +0.95 pt from the market, +0.26 pt from the cybersecurity industry (CIBR) and +0.27 pt company-specific (z-score 0.17). There is no company-specific move to explain. Over the past 5 days (+7.1%), almost all of the move (+7.04 pt) was the industry.
No company press release or 8-K landed in the window. The only company-specific items were pre-planned insider sales disclosed after the close on Friday, which cannot explain Friday's move.

Why cybersecurity stocks as a group rose this week: not established. The search budget ran out before an industry-level search could run. Commentary in tier-3 coverage links the sector rally to enthusiasm for 'AI-driven cybersecurity demand'.

Longer-run driver of the +130% year-to-date move: management credits AI adoption for faster growth ('The Mythos moment translated into mass-market acceptance that AI adoption needs security'). Net new ARR grew 51% YoY in Q2 and FY27 guidance was raised.

Much of the price rise is valuation expansion (investors paying more per dollar of sales), not only growth. Trefis puts the stock at about 50x trailing sales against about 3x for the S&P 500, and Zacks puts it at 39x forward sales.

products.name: Falcon Flex
products.what_it_is: A flexible way to buy CrowdStrike: the customer commits a budget up front and can switch on any Falcon modules later without signing a new contract each time.
products.analogy: Like a prepaid gift card for a whole shopping mall instead of a receipt for one shop.
products.buyers: Mid-size and large companies that already use some CrowdStrike modules.
products.how_it_works: The customer signs a larger multi-module commitment, then draws it down by deploying modules such as cloud security, identity protection or Next-Gen SIEM as needed.
products.sales: Ending ARR from accounts that have adopted Falcon Flex exceeded $2.29 billion as of 2026-07-31, up 101% YoY
products.size_for_company: Falcon Flex accounts make up about 39% of total ARR ($2.29B of $5.84B). Note this is ARR of all accounts that adopted Flex, not ARR sold through Flex alone.
products.competition: Palo Alto Networks (platform bundles), Microsoft Defender (bundled with Microsoft 365), SentinelOne
products.why_investors_care: It is the mechanism behind 'customers keep adding modules' (thesis pillar 1).
products.watch_next: Flex ARR and its growth rate in the Q3 FY27 release (expected early December 2026)

products.name: Falcon on the OpenAI Marketplace
products.what_it_is: A new way to buy CrowdStrike: through OpenAI's enterprise marketplace, paid for with money a company has already committed to spend with OpenAI.
products.analogy: Like being able to spend your airline miles at a partner hotel.
products.how_it_works: The customer applies part of an existing OpenAI commitment to a Falcon purchase. The launch is paired with Falcon Guardian (runtime protection for OpenAI Codex AI agents) and a FAIRR readiness service.
products.size_for_company: not disclosed. Proxy: total ARR was $5.84B at 2026-07-31; no channel breakdown is given.
products.competition: Other security vendors on cloud and AI marketplaces (e.g. AWS Marketplace); Microsoft security bundled with its own AI stack
products.why_investors_care: It lowers the friction of buying CrowdStrike for companies already spending big on AI, which fits management's 'AI needs security' story.
products.watch_next: Whether management cites OpenAI Marketplace deals or Falcon Guardian ARR on the Q3 call
